speakers: Tom Roble (SG Prime Services, SG CTA indices)
summary:
Top Traders Unplugged Systematic Investor 339 (March 2025): CTA index performance, regime and time-frame diversification, stacked managed-futures products, replication versus managers and BlackRock's ETF entry.
Conclusions: trend and broad CTA indices are nearly the same; short-term models help only at inflections; replication and ETFs are not a threat except BlackRock; bonds' failure as diversifier drives trend demand.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you've got to stretch the tails out and and and it's going to be an unbelievable ride from here and uh you know good or bad um volatility is here
claims.claim: The new US administration's willingness to stress systems widens the range of macro and market outcomes, so fat tails and higher volatility should be expected.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they basically uh say that the last 15 years have been the best 15-year period at any in any time um since 1970
claims.claim: Bridgewater found the last 15 years the best 15-year equity period since 1970, which makes it hard for non-equity strategies to attract capital and raises the chance that equity returns are near a high.
claims.conditions: after exceptional runs future returns may be lower

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: percentage of US household that holds uh equities is something like 80 82%
claims.claim: US households hold equities at about 80 to 82%, so a market high could be widely felt.
claims.indicator: share of US households holding equities (~82%)

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: my own trend barometer finished at 57. Now, for those who follow it, they will know that that's actually a pretty good reading
claims.claim: Niels's Trend Barometer at 57 signals a good environment for trend following after a weak start to 2025.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: the flagship sort of broad SGCTA index is currently down just over 2 and a half% for the year
claims.claim: In March 2025 the SG CTA Index was down about 2.5% YTD (down nearly 1% in March) and the SG Trend Index down about 4.5% YTD, drifting sideways early in the year.
claims.indicator: SG CTA Index, SG Trend Index

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: increased volatility as something that a lot of these CTA groups look for and and in and have historically done done very well in
claims.claim: Higher volatility and emerging trends are what CTAs historically profit from, so rising volatility improves their outlook.
claims.direction: CTAs gain from volatility expansion that produces trends
claims.testable: yes - CTA returns vs volatility regimes

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: they have a 98% correlation and the trend is like a 1.2 1.3 version of the other
claims.claim: The SG Trend Index and the broader SG CTA Index are 98% correlated, with trend roughly 1.2-1.3 times the broad index, so the roughly 2% annual 5-year gap is mostly leverage and replicating either is equally feasible.
claims.indicator: SG CTA Index vs SG Trend Index correlation 0.98

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it it really has to do with the the the pendulum in terms of whether trend is cool or not cool
claims.claim: The popularity of trend following versus broader managed futures swings like a pendulum: trend was seen as dead in the mid-2010s, then outperformed from March 2020 through 2022, which reshaped what investors want.
claims.indicator: trend vs broad managed futures relative performance

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you would expect the sharp ratio of the of the broader index to be meaningfully higher
claims.claim: If non-trend components added meaningful value the broad index would show a clearly higher Sharpe than the trend index, which Andrew does not see; Sharpe in the space has stayed flat or declined over 20 years.
claims.indicator: Sharpe of SG CTA vs SG Trend; Sharpe of the space

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: this month, you know, is actually a pretty strong positive month for our short-term traders index. So, it's up over 1%
claims.claim: In March 2025 the SG Short-Term Traders Index rose over 1% and broke from lockstep with trend and CTA indices, producing the first real dispersion among them that year, linked to model time frame.
claims.direction: short-term models outperform in sharp reversals

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: they all do different things around the periphery and that can often make a big difference
claims.claim: Trend followers show very high correlations because trend is the dominant factor, yet performance dispersion arises from differences around the periphery (universe, sizing, speed), as in equities.
claims.testable: partly - dispersion attribution needs manager data

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: S&P 500 total return down 7.21% as of yesterday down almost 6% so far this year
claims.claim: In March 2025 equities sold off (S&P 500 TR down 7.21% in the month, almost 6% YTD) while the US aggregate bond index was up 2% YTD.
claims.indicator: S&P 500 TR, MSCI World, S&P US Aggregate Bond

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: European and some Asian markets are actually doing well for trend followers and then US markets are not doing uh very well for for for managers
claims.claim: Trend P&L in early 2025 diverged within sectors: European and Asian equities, JGBs, gold and silver worked, while US equities, other bonds and currencies lost, which is unusual.
claims.direction: long EU/Asian equities, short JGB yields, long gold

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: our portfolio is by design very uscentric in terms of the instruments that we use
claims.claim: A replication portfolio built on US-centric instruments missed diversification in March 2025 (e.g. euro vs dollar, Bunds, JGBs) and underperformed the broad index, ending closer to the trend index; diversification helped actual CTAs.
claims.conditions: months when non-US markets drive trend P&L

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: hedge funds started to dial up the Trump trade and and you saw it in fundamental hedge funds you saw it in CTAs
claims.claim: Hedge funds and CTAs crowded into a post-election consensus (long equities, strong dollar, sticky inflation, long gold) that reversed in early 2025, producing losses.
claims.conditions: consensus positioning reversing on policy news

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: when hedge funds generate alpha and this in it picks up CTAs as well you have to do something that's contrarian right
claims.claim: Alpha requires deviating from consensus and being early on information shifts rather than merely following price; the largest alpha comes from shifts in information such as betting markets pricing a changed election outcome.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: most allocators cannot change their portfolios fast on that basis. They do annual rebalancings.
claims.claim: Allocators rebalance annually with long-term assumptions, so flexible macro managers and CTAs have an edge in reacting to big information changes.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: The part that doesn't work is when sentiment flip-flops back and forth around the same trade.
claims.claim: Rapid oscillations of sentiment hurt short-term traders in some cases and long-term traders in others, so chaotic flip-flops are hard for anything against the market grain.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: it must be easier all things being equal to be a systematic rules-based manager um just following whatever actually takes place in the markets
claims.claim: Following markets systematically is easier than predicting both policy and market reaction, which a fool's errand would require.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: It brings something to a a a traditional portfolio that you really cannot and should not be doing on your own
claims.claim: Managed futures is a completion strategy whose value comes from the diversification it adds to a traditional portfolio, not from standalone Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: that is the ideal 6 month 9 month 12-month trade for CTAs
claims.claim: If a recession-driven fall in yields occurred, CTAs would quickly flip from sticky-inflation shorts to long Treasuries, an ideal multi-month trade where systematic adaptability pays off.
claims.indicator: Treasury yields in a deep recession scenario
claims.conditions: scenario only: a recession engineered to cut yields

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: the only thing you can be sure of is that your timing is going to be completely wrong
claims.claim: Investors struggle to hold diversifiers: with negative correlation to equities during an unbelievable equity run you give something up, and timing will be wrong, so evaluate over long periods including upside.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: we're seeing more and more interest in portable alpha where we're seeing much more efficient use of a portfolio capital to generate returns
claims.claim: Portable alpha overlays diversifiers on top of full equity exposure, so investors protect the left tail without giving up the equity right tail.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: where there has been growth is managed futures with equities bolted onto it
claims.claim: Mutual fund AUM in managed futures has been flat, but stacked products (equities plus managed futures, e.g. Catalyst about $8bn at 200bp) are growing.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the best thing you can do from a marketing perspective is just slapping on the one index that has been going on uh going up for for for 15 years
claims.claim: Combining equities with managed futures is a marketing cycle: it was prepared in the 1990s but dropped when equities went sideways for 10 years after 2000, and may fade when equities stop rising.
claims.testable: partly - product launches vs equity returns

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: if I take it from equities, clients are going to blame me if equities go up.
claims.claim: Advisers cannot easily fund a managed futures allocation from equities or bonds because clients will blame them if the source asset outperforms.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: there will be moments and this is actually one of those moments where they're both going to both skis are going to go down at the same time
claims.claim: Stacked equity plus trend products suffer when both fall together (e.g. S&P -6% and trend -4% = -10% in a month), which is hard to explain to risk-averse clients for a zero long-term beta strategy.
claims.conditions: sharp equity sell-off with trend reversal

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you take a very very cheap efficient equity allocation and you tend to make it tax inefficient and expensive
claims.claim: Wrapping an ETF equity position in a mutual fund destroys its tax efficiency (ETFs avoid realized gains) and adds fees.
claims.indicator: ETF vs mutual fund tax efficiency

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you have to mark into market every year
claims.claim: Getting equity exposure via futures in the US triggers annual mark-to-market taxation (around 30% on some), further eroding tax efficiency of stacked products.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: which is the 5-year line item risk of owning managed futures when equities are going up
claims.claim: Some advisers accept friction of stacked products because it removes the career or line-item risk of holding managed futures when equities rise, even if not optimal on Sharpe, tax or fees.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: this sort of clash between your strategic asset allocation and your tactical asset allocation, which something like a portable alpha product potentially solves
claims.claim: Portable alpha lets tactical diversifier positions coexist with strategic allocation without moving dollars between asset classes.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: regime identification seems to be something that a lot of groups are focused spending a lot of time on applying a lot of different statistical methods
claims.claim: CTAs invest research in regime detection to adjust risk across model sets or add fundamental or carry strategies when long-term trends are weak.
claims.testable: yes - regime filters testable but prone to overfitting

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: CTA's had one of their worst days I mean for a long long long time and of course there's no way of no no regime mechanism would predict uh that
claims.claim: Omicron news in late 2021 caused a CTA worst day yet began one of the strongest runs (2022), showing regime filters cannot predict shocks and tinkering risks losing the strategy's value.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: what they can do is then quickly and much be much more rapid in adapting to the new regime
claims.claim: Regime models cannot avoid sudden shifts but can identify a new regime and adapt faster.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: then have more of a constant allocation across those different models
claims.claim: A naive alternative to regime timing is to run several model time frames with a roughly constant allocation across them.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: what we think it more is is that CTAs are employing many more models and they are using some sort of methodology to try and allocate risk across those different models
claims.claim: Rather than simply lengthening horizons, CTAs now run many more models and allocate risk across them; the SG Trend indicator keeps a medium-term model for consistency.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: the shorterterm models have delivered significantly positive returns during those periods but then for the interim the longerterm models are very very strong of their performance
claims.claim: Short-term models profit at major inflection points (GFC, COVID, Ukraine war) while long-term models dominate in the intervals, so having both lets a CTA adapt.
claims.indicator: short-term vs long-term trend model returns
claims.direction: short models at breakouts; long models in persistent trends

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you look great in one out of four periods and your sharp ratio is zero
claims.claim: Shorter models do better at inflection points by definition, but over most periods their Sharpe is lower, so they help only a fraction of the time.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: And the two costs are you're paying 100 basis points more for it. You've got an indetermined amount of additional costs associated with trading hundreds or thousands of, you know, individual contracts
claims.claim: Faster, more diversified CTA programs (e.g. American Beacon/Man AHL) cost about 100bp more plus extra trading costs and likely lower Sharpe, despite better drawdown control and inflection performance.
claims.indicator: fees and trading costs of broad vs simple programs

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: tell me your best idea 3 years ago, your best idea 3 years before that, your best idea 3 years before that
claims.claim: Due diligence test for managers introducing new model features: ask why not earlier and for the best idea of each past period; innovations arrive because something wasn't working.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the signal is whether the S&P is going to go up or down
claims.claim: An index track record with an unrealistically high Sharpe from adding a QIS timing overlay (doubling Sharpe) usually hides an unavailable signal such as predicting the S&P; if real, one would just trade the market itself.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we allow our models to recalibrate themselves so that the parameters and and let's just think about look back period as the only parameter here
claims.claim: Rather than committee-picked time frames, models can recalibrate their lookback systematically; Niels also runs a yearly analysis of the best-performing time frame from a few weeks to about 2.5 years.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: longer time frames tend to cluster meaning that you might have five or six years
claims.claim: The best-performing trend lookback clusters over multiple years (five to seven years of 200-day-plus), not only because of AUM-driven slowing, so lookback regimes persist.
claims.indicator: best trend lookback by calendar year

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: the clustering became less than a 100 days
claims.claim: After the GFC the best time frame clustered below 100 days for about five years, and in 2008 the best absolute time frame was about 56 days, before longer horizons returned.
claims.indicator: best trend lookback by year (2008: 56 days)

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: where we also want to dynamically allocate our risk because even though it's not an exact science there are certain things you can pick up
claims.claim: Dynamic risk allocation using trend-environment indicators (e.g. Trend Barometer) can modestly improve results as long as one does not over-predict the future or trade the same way regardless of environment.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: certain short-term strategies are looking for that kind of um breakout of volatility and and and and the persistence of that volatility they can capture that very effectively
claims.claim: Short-term strategies profit from volatility breakouts when the volatility persists, so a manager needs execution expertise and low slippage to flip positions quickly.
claims.testable: yes - vol persistence and short-term P&L

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: making a 10-year bet right if you think you're going to have this as an allocation for 10 years you're making a very very specific bet the industry is not going to change
claims.claim: Bottom-up replication indices work at first then drift as the industry evolves, whereas Andrew's top-down replication is adaptive because it targets current industry positioning.
claims.testable: yes - correlation to index over time

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's designed to be a very very short-term bet on where they're positioned on a Monday
claims.claim: Replication is a short-horizon bet on weekly industry positioning; it has stably high correlation over long periods and is rebalanced weekly using weighted data (3 current and 17 stale points).

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: I've never seen a period even through some of these very very sharp inflection points where the industry goes from 100% long to 100% short
claims.claim: In sharp shocks vol controls make managers derisk faster than a weekly replicator (e.g. 100 to 70 vs replicator 180 to 100), but the industry never flips fully, so residual lag is bounded.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: you get a lot of false positives that go off or or or you kind of cut risk at the wrong time
claims.claim: Sharp short-lived volatility spikes (three-day wall spikes, like the yen carry unwind) trigger false vol-control signals and cut risk at the wrong time, adding volatility without clearly hurting long-term Sharpe.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: There is definitely signs that during stressful periods the correlation breaks more so on the index replicator than on the mechanical replicator.
claims.claim: Index-based replicators lose correlation to the benchmark more in stress periods than mechanical bottom-up replicators.
claims.indicator: correlation of replicators to index in stress

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it is very hard to pick one trend person and end up with the reliable representation
claims.claim: Single-manager trend selections vary more over time than the replicator versus index, so replication is a structural-alpha tradeoff against noise.
claims.indicator: dispersion of single managers vs index

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: according to Barkley Heads, there's 330 or 340 billion of assets across the space, right? The managed futures ETF space is 3 billion
claims.claim: Managed futures ETFs hold about $3bn of the roughly $330-340bn in the space and have grown 10x in 5-6 years, so they are not a big threat except BlackRock's entry.
claims.indicator: managed futures AUM ($330-340bn) and ETF AUM ($3bn)

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the typical allocator to hedge funds does not buy generally does not buy an ETF
claims.claim: Hedge fund allocators prefer prestigious hedge funds over ETFs, so ETF growth will come from new investors, not cannibalise CTAs.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's priced at 80 basis points which is a bit higher than I thought they were going to come in
claims.claim: BlackRock's managed futures ETF at 80bp with 40-50 instruments is not cheap versus institutional mandates, QIS products or typical ETFs (80% below 25bp), while mutual funds at 150-250bp are expensive.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: But if you're buying a specific ETF, say a trend following ETF, I really don't think you're buying it to save 20 or 30 basis points compared to another manager
claims.claim: Fee savings matter for index replication but not when selecting a single manager with a long track record that has outperformed the index by several hundred basis points.
claims.testable: partly - depends on persistence of manager alpha

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: a typical alligator out there already has money with them and already has a 10 or 20 year old correct it's like an access kind of route
claims.claim: PIMCO became the largest US managed futures mutual fund through existing client relationships and a good March 2020, not trend expertise, then underperformed in 2022 after raising assets.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: they had designed their strategy to be much more sensitive to equity sell-offs
claims.claim: PIMCO's program was designed to be more sensitive to equity sell-offs, explaining its underperformance in 2022.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: alternative markets, oh, they trend better, right? And they had a two or three years where they did well relative to the other developed market managers
claims.claim: The argument that alternative markets trend better produced 2-3 good years then 3-4 underperformance years, warning against chasing shiny new ideas.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: They launch it expecting to a 6% return with a 6% standard deviation, no correlation, anything, and it goes down 35%.
claims.claim: BlackRock Style Advantage fund (alternative risk premia) targeted 6% return and volatility but lost 35%, fell from $2.5bn to $250m, showing big firms can fail; wait for a 3 to 5 year track record.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: Let them have a three or five year track record. Show them that for for three or five years and then make the call.
claims.claim: Allocators should wait for 3-5 years of live track record for new products from large firms rather than rush.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: I would always choose someone who has experience over someone who just has size
claims.claim: Experience beats size when choosing CTA managers.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: it's going to legitimize manageers as an asset class
claims.claim: BlackRock's launch may legitimise managed futures in wealth management, though platforms may then only use BlackRock.

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: in the Barkclay report when they report on on AUM they actually include Bridgewwater's two products right
claims.claim: Barclay managed futures AUM data include Bridgewater's two products, which fell from about $145bn (Feb 2021) to about $97bn, so stagnant industry AUM may reflect one firm's decline.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: the competitive threat then was was banks you know and banks offering QIS products
claims.claim: The competitive threat to hedge funds a decade ago was banks offering cheap QIS products, whose performance and fees are not visible, making comparison unfair.

claims.speaker: Tom Roble
claims.quote: it's a typically a different buyer of the product
claims.claim: QIS products are bought by smaller to large groups for tactical trades (e.g. a curve steepener with continual delta hedging) rather than the hedge fund team, so money isn't coming from traditional hedge fund allocations.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: precisely because bonds stopped working as a diversifier
claims.claim: After 2022 more investors adopt trend following because bonds stopped diversifying equities, undermining the stock-bond relationships on which asset allocation models rely.
claims.direction: more demand for trend as a diversifier

claims.speaker: Niels Kaastrup-Larsen
claims.quote: we're in the best environment for macro investing we've probably seen for the last 10 years
claims.claim: Geopolitical dislocations, volatility and uncertain inflation make 2025 the best environment for macro and CTA investing in a decade.

claims.speaker: Andrew Beer
claims.quote: one of the the the star um ETFs is is called CTA, and it's really only commodities with a little bit of I think they have a little bit of interest rates
claims.claim: A star ETF labelled CTA holds essentially only commodities and some rates, showing the CTA label is loosely used and its recent returns reflect a commodity run.
